paper_title: On Weak epsilon-Nets and the Radon Number
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 4
statement: In Section 1.4, we provide an example showing that the compactness assumption in Corollary 3 is necessary. We do not know if the separability assumption is necessary.
context: The proof of Corollary 3 appears in Section 4.1. It shows that the role of the Radon number in the existence of weak nets is similar to the role of the VC dimension in the existence of strong nets, at least for separable compact convexity spaces. In Section 1.4, we provide an example showing that the compactness assumption in Corollary 3 is necessary. We do not know if the separability assumption is necessary. The implication 2 ⇒ 3 in Corollary 3 is an amplification statement for the parameter  in weak nets. In Section 4.2 we give an example showing that the threshold 1/2 in item 2 is sharp for amplification of weak nets: I Example 4. There is a compact separable convexity space that has weak -nets of finite size for every  > 1/2 but has no weak -nets of finite size for  < 21 .
